findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout.
findings.fix: Rewrite the opening sentence to state the topic the rest of the paragraph covers.
findings.violation: The paragraph's opening sentence shares almost no vocabulary with the rest of the paragraph, so it does not preview the paragraph's actual topic.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.fix: Delete the unrelated sentences, or move them to a separate section. If you must include them, create a new section titled 'General Updates' or similar and explain their relevance.
findings.violation: The section opens with a governing topic (benefits team coordinating stipend requests) but immediately shifts to three completely unrelated topics (travel expense audit, remote work guidance, coffee budget reset) with no connection back to the main topic.

findings.evidence: You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review. Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days. You track its status there until the payment clears.
findings.fix: Separate the employee instructions from the internal process descriptions, or clearly label which sentences apply to which audience.
findings.violation: The section addresses multiple audiences without clear separation. It mixes employee instructions ('You record...', 'you submit...', 'You track...') with process descriptions for other roles ('Finance reconciles...', 'Payroll releases...') and a manager instruction ('Countersign the employee request...'), making it unclear which sentences are meant for the reader.

findings.evidence: In Eligibility: 'the stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year'. In How to Apply: 'Employees start a stipend request in the benefits portal'.
findings.fix: Choose one term consistently throughout the document, or explicitly state that 'claim' and 'request' are equivalent.
findings.location: Eligibility and How to Apply sections
findings.violation: The term 'claim' in the Eligibility section and 'request' throughout the rest of the document refer to the same concept (what an employee submits to receive the stipend) but are used inconsistently with no signal that they are equivalent.

findings.fix: Move the interrupting clause elsewhere, or split it into its own sentence.
